risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Frequent, ad hoc changes to drug-pricing rules create uncertainty for long-term investment planning, R&D and product launches.
- As an exporter, the company flags currency volatility, logistical disruptions and differing country regulations as pressures on cost structures and market-entry timelines.
- M&A-driven consolidation and players crowding into semi-urban and rural markets are expected to raise saturation and price competition in generic formulations, pressuring mid-sized homegrown companies.
- Management cites these, with supply-chain disruptions, as having moderated industry growth to about 7-8% CAGR; domestic compliance standards are also evolving.
- Public health expenditure near 1% of GDP and low insurance cover leave most patients paying out-of-pocket, limiting drug access and compliance, especially for chronic therapies.
- Limited doctors and health workers, especially in rural and semi-urban areas, lowers diagnosis and prescription rates and so medicine demand.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Diversify from a formulations-focused manufacturer into adjacent healthcare, medical-technology, defence and AI areas through nine newly incorporated subsidiaries.
- Build out the Medical Technology vertical: FY2025-26 was spent aggregating key resources and supply chains, with operations kept minimal by choice.
- Expand footprint in regulated and semi-regulated export markets, diversify product offerings and enhance strategic collaborations.
- Evaluate new formulations, dosage variations and therapeutic-class expansion in chronic-disease segments, aligning product development and capacity planning …
